e. (Page 19) Care should be taken to insure that, with the opening of certain areas to ORV use, the user does not come to think that all areas of the public lands are open to the use of his vehicle.

f. (Page 26) On this page a paragraph states: "Within designated ORV areas some irreversible or irretrievable impacts upon land forms, wildlife and their habitat, and historical and archeological sites may occur despite the utmost of precautions." Again careful attention should be focused upon the criteria of areas zoned for ORV use to hold their cultural and environmental impact to a minimum.
It seems that any recreational form that becomes popular and economical will be welcomed to the public lands. Accepting this fact leads one to wonder, should the average citizen find himself capable of purchasing bulldozers and army surplus tanks, will he be allowed access with these vehicles to the public lands?
It is good to see that the Department of the Interior recognizes the problem that ORV's create and is trying to regulate their use. These regulations should be carefully analyzed and strictly enforced to insure the perpetuation and undiminished integrity of our public lands.
Sincerely,
Walter L. Criley
Joe Gaines
Project Administrator
